cast.name: Mohan
cast.appearsAs: a weathered man in his seventies, lean and stooped, with deep lines, in a faded cotton kurta

acting.masterProfile: Mohan moves with a low center of gravity, his weight settled in the heels and his shoulders drawn forward as if carrying the boat’s weight. His tempo is slow and economical; each step lands before the next begins, and his hands stay close to his body unless they are working. His breath is shallow and audible in cold air, and he pauses after a line before letting his eyes return to the task. His hands are his main instrument: they smooth, press, and test surfaces, and when pressure rises his right thumb rubs the side of his left palm twice. Under the trigger of Tarun’s direct statement, his jaw tightens, his blink rate drops, and his hands stop moving for a beat before he acts. He wears a mask of quiet routine, keeping his gaze on the boat, the cloth, or the water rather than on his son. The crack appears as a stillness in the chest and a slight drop of the head, followed by one deliberate hand movement. His eye life is steady: he tracks the boat’s line, lets micro-saccades follow the water’s edge, blinks slowly, and keeps catchlights alive in the low dawn light. He leads with the eyes first, then the hands, then the voice.

cast.name: Tarun
cast.appearsAs: a man in his forties, lean and upright, with a short beard, in a pressed shirt

acting.masterProfile: Tarun stands with a high center of gravity, his shoulders squared and his weight balanced evenly, as if he has been away from this place. His movement is controlled and deliberate; he stops before the boat, keeps his arms close, and lets his hands settle only when he has a reason to move. His breath is even, but his chest rises a little faster when he speaks. His hands are his pressure point: they hover near his shirt pocket, then drop to his sides, and when he receives the oar his fingers close slowly around the wood. Under the trigger of taking the oar, his jaw sets, his blink rate slows, and his head turns toward the boat before his body follows. He wears a mask of calm practicality, keeping his face level and his words short. The crack appears as a small tremor in the hands and a half-second pause before he grips the oar. His eye life is alert: he scans the mist, the boat, and his father’s face, with quick micro-saccades and live catchlights in the low dawn light. He leads with the eyes, then the hands, then the feet.
